pages.lesson:
LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS , IMITATIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.6: Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we build our vocabulary?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify information from audio texts for communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS , IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS , IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify information from audio texts for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify information from audio texts for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify information from audio texts for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify information from audio texts for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify information from audio texts for communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify information from audio texts for communication.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we build our vocabulary?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonological awareness , Imitative speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify information from audio texts for communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
